oleate and linoleate are esterified to the same lipid, that linoleate is esterified more quickly than oleate, and that linoleate desatration is a two-step process, with the initial desaturation occurring on the same lipid to which oleate was esterified.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oleate and linoleate are esterified in phosphatidyl choline and then desaturate in the phosphatidyl-choline fraction.
oleate and linoleate desatration in cucumber cotyledons occur on phosphatidyl choline and that the pathway of linoleate and alpha-linolenate esterification is triacylglycerol-galactolipids.
oleate is esterified to PC, then converted to linoleate, and that linoleate esterified to PG is then converted to linolenate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oleate and linoleate esterified to PC is the initial site for desaturation of oleate to linoleate, which is subsequently transferred to the other acyl lipids.
oleate desaturation in cucumber seedlings is a two-step process involving initial esterification to phosphatidylethanolamine and subsequent transfer to other lipid classes.
the initial esterification of oleate and linoleate occurs in phosphatidyl-choline and the subsequent desaturation occurs in monogalactosyldiacylglycerol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oleate is desaturated to linoleate prior to incorporation into galactolipid.
oleate and linoleate esterified to PC is desaturated to linoleate prior to esterification to other lipids.
the pathway for fatty acid desaturation in cucumber cotyledons is different from what has been described in other plants.
